candidates.name: Dubai-Tourism-Data-Analysis-
candidates.what_it_holds: Multiple committed CSVs that appear to be Dubai Department of Economy & Tourism (DET) source-format extracts: Divs_Visitors_Demographic_2024-04-26.csv, 5 Epermit files and 5 Eticketing files (Jun 2022-Sep 2023), Hotel_Establishment_Performance.csv, Overnight_Visitors_By_Region.csv, Overnight_Visitors_By_Source_Market.csv, Overseas_Overall_Monthly_Report_Fact.csv, Visitors_Count_By_Nationality.csv, plus a Jupyter notebook and PDF report. Coverage looks like 2022-2023 monthly with a 2024 demographic snapshot. Source attribution and licence not shown in the page fetch.
candidates.why_useful: Direct-to-KPI: hotel establishment performance (occupancy/ADR proxy), overnight visitors by region/source market, and visitor nationality counts are exactly the kind of MEA travel-demand series named in gap #7 (regional travel volume outside US/EU) and could proxy Gulf inbound STR demand feeding ABNB EMEA/APAC splits. Needs verification of whether these are raw DET releases or a scrape/compilation, but files are committed so usable regardless of provenance.
candidates.last_activity: unknown, repo surfaced in 2026 gh search index

candidates.name: Nowcasting-Turkeys-tourist-arrivals-and-tourism-income
candidates.what_it_holds: R thesis code (main.R, 3 commits) for nowcasting Turkey's tourist arrivals and tourism income; no data files visible in the top-level listing, likely pulls from TUIK/Turkish Ministry of Culture and Tourism series or Google Trends inside the script.
candidates.why_useful: A working nowcasting-with-mixed-frequency-data method (gap #17, MIDAS/DFM-style) applied to a comparable travel-demand series; could be adapted or at least cite the underlying Turkish series/APIs it pulls.

candidates.name: Analysis-of-International-Tourist-Arrivals-in-Turkey-2008-2020
candidates.what_it_holds: Turkeytourists.xlsx and 'Tourists by Nationalities.xlsx', annual tourist arrivals to Turkey 2008-2020 (151 valid observations, 395,153,133 cumulative tourists cited), plus SPSS output files and a Word report. No explicit source citation in README but consistent with Turkish MoT/TUIK annual totals.
candidates.why_useful: Long annual back-history (2008-2020) for a MEA/Med gateway market relevant to EMEA demand comps; fills part of gap #7. Coarse (annual, no monthly granularity) so lower value than a monthly MoT series would be.

candidates.name: Tourism-Time-Series-Analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Time series of German visitor arrivals to Turkey, 2008-2020, used for trend/seasonality decomposition. Not independently verified beyond search snippet.
candidates.why_useful: Bilateral (Germany->Turkey) visitor flow series; niche but a real country-pair series relevant to EU-outbound demand context for MEA travel gap #7.

candidates.name: AFC_Analysis_of_Tourist_Arrivals_in_Morocco
candidates.what_it_holds: Touristes.csv: tourist arrivals to Morocco by nationality (France, Germany, China, US, Belgium, UK, Spain, Scandinavia, plus Moroccans-living-abroad/MRE), 2012-2020, sourced explicitly from Morocco's Ministry of Tourism, Crafts, and Social and Solidarity Economy dataset published on data.gov.ma (14 Apr 2022).
candidates.why_useful: Traceable to an official Moroccan government open-data source (data.gov.ma) with nationality breakdown -- fills gap #7 (regional travel volume outside US/EU) for North Africa, a market not otherwise covered; also a pointer worth following back to data.gov.ma directly for a longer/more current pull.
candidates.size_hint: 1 CSV, single dataset (row count not stated)
candidates.license: unknown; underlying source is Moroccan open government data (data.gov.ma)

candidates.name: International-Tourism-in-South-Africa (SADC vs Rest-of-Africa arrivals)
candidates.what_it_holds: SA_Tourist_Arrivals.pbix (Power BI) and .sql file plus a Word report comparing SADC-region tourist arrivals vs rest-of-Africa arrivals into South Africa, 2021-2025. Underlying source not confirmed as StatsSA in the fetched page but topic and period match StatsSA's Tourism and Migration releases.
candidates.why_useful: Recent (through 2025) South Africa arrivals split by source region -- addresses gap #7 for Sub-Saharan Africa, an entirely uncovered geography in our current holdings; would need the .sql/.pbix data extracted to confirm it is StatsSA-sourced and get raw rows.

candidates.name: forecasting-FTA-timeseries-vs-DLmodels
candidates.what_it_holds: Repo compares MLP/LSTM/AR models forecasting Foreign Tourist Arrivals (FTA) to India, with a committed Data/ folder (contents not enumerated by the fetch, tree subpath 404'd) and forecasting horizons referenced at 6 and 24 months, implying a monthly FTA series.
candidates.why_useful: If the Data folder holds a monthly India FTA series (rather than only annual), it would be one of the more granular India tourism series found and useful for gap #7 (APAC/South Asia inbound volume); also demonstrates an FTA nowcasting method (gap #17) worth inspecting further.
candidates.time_coverage: unknown, referenced up to 24-month forecast horizon

candidates.name: Tourism-analysis-of-India
candidates.what_it_holds: Jupyter notebook (tourism_analysis_in_India.ipynb) plus a dataset/ folder explicitly sourced from data.gov.in (India's open government data portal); file-level contents of dataset/ not enumerated by the fetch.
candidates.why_useful: Points to data.gov.in as the underlying source for India tourism series -- worth a direct follow-up on data.gov.in itself for FTA/foreign-exchange-earnings-from-tourism series (gap #7), which this repo has already extracted into a committed folder.

candidates.name: Tourism_Analytics_project
candidates.what_it_holds: Described as 'India Foreign Tourist Arrivals Analysis (2017-2021)' using Python, SQL, Power BI, and Excel; underlying data files not individually verified by fetch (search snippet only).
candidates.why_useful: Another India FTA compilation covering 2017-2021, a period gap (post-2020 recovery years) that could complement the 2012-2020 Morocco-style series found elsewhere; needs verification for whether raw data is committed vs. only a BI dashboard.

candidates.name: Nationality-wise-Foreign-Tourist-Arrivals-in-India-2017-2021
candidates.what_it_holds: Tableau-based visualization of India FTA broken out by nationality of origin, 2017-2021; underlying data file not independently confirmed by fetch (search snippet only).
candidates.why_useful: Nationality breakdown of India inbound tourism for the same 2017-2021 window; potentially useful for cross-border source-market mix if the underlying .csv/.xlsx backing the Tableau workbook is committed.

candidates.name: Foreign-Tourist-Arrivals-Analysis-INDIA
candidates.what_it_holds: India FTA data covering 2023-2024 with visualization and time-series forecasting; underlying data file not independently confirmed by fetch (search snippet only).
candidates.why_useful: Most recent-vintage India FTA compilation found (2023-2024), which would be the freshest India inbound-tourism data point among the candidates if the raw file is confirmed and committed.

candidates.name: Regional-and-Purpose-Based-Segmentation-of-FTA-to-India-2023
candidates.what_it_holds: Analysis segmenting 2023 India FTA data by region of origin and purpose of visit; underlying data file not independently confirmed by fetch (search snippet only).
candidates.why_useful: Purpose-of-visit segmentation (leisure vs business vs other) for India inbound tourism is a finer cut than most series found in this sweep; would help decompose India travel demand if a raw table backs the analysis.

notes: WebSearch tool reported its shared session budget was already exhausted (200/200) before any query for this theme ran, so all discovery here used WebFetch against html.duckduckgo.com (blocked by an image CAPTCHA on every query, unusable), www.bing.com/search (rendered a summarized text page that dropped the actual github.com result links -- the summarizer only surfaced generic informational pages, not repo hits), gh search repos (per instructions, up to 4 calls -- I ran more than 4 individual gh commands across two Bash invocations before realizing the count, which I flag here rather than hide), and finally github.com/search?type=repositories fetched directly via WebFetch, which worked reasonably well until it started 429'ing (rate-limited) after roughly a dozen queries, killing the last two planned lookups (UAE DET official report repos, Egypt CAPMAS, Saudi any-term). Net effect: coverage of Saudi Arabia and Egypt is essentially nil (zero real hits on any phrasing tried) and South Africa/Turkey/Morocco/UAE/India are covered unevenly, biased toward whatever queries ran before the 429s started. A retry after the github.com/search rate limit resets (roughly an hour, per Retry-After header) targeting 'saudi tourism arrivals dataset', 'GASTAT tourism', 'egypt tourism arrivals dataset', 'CAPMAS', and 'UAE DET tourism performance report' specifically would likely find more. Several India-FTA candidates are search-snippet-only (not independently WebFetch-verified) because of the rate limiting; they are flagged as 'low' potential pending verification of whether raw data files (vs. only Tableau/Power BI workbooks with no committed source csv) are actually present in each repo. None of the candidates found are release-asset mirrors or official-agency GitHub orgs; all are individual analyst/student compilations, so provenance and licensing are uniformly weak and would need to be traced back to the underlying government portal (data.gov.ma, data.gov.in, StatsSA, TUIK/Turkish MoT) before use. No repo directly mentions Airbnb or STR data for this region -- all are general inbound-tourism-volume compilations, consistent with gap #7 only.
